Cc: procurement@faberhealth.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MSA redlines - defense control and evidence onboarding

Hi Ava —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached are Faber's initial redlines to the MSA (see attached PDF). Two items our procurement/legal teams flagged that we need to resolve before we can proceed to procurement approval:

1) Defense control for third-party IP claims: Faber's legal prefers customer-led defense with the right to control the litigation and select counsel.

2) Evidence & data retention onboarding: we need a named point of contact and SLA for producing technical evidence (logs, model inputs) if a claim arises.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept customer defense control with (a) prompt notice, (b) Redwood cooperation, and (c) a limited carveout for Redwood to step in if customer direction would prejudice Redwood's rights? Also attaching our evidence onboarding template — procurement wants to lock the timeline.

We'd like to get this wrapped this week so procurement can route the PO.

Alyssa Park

Alyssa —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. I've looped in our legal lead Kimberly and our Ops/infra lead Connor so we can confirm. Preliminary answers:

- Notice / cooperation: yes, we can accept prompt notice and a cooperation clause.
- Defense control: customer-led defense is common, but our Legal will want a structured "defense control" carve that preserves Redwood's right to participate and to approve settlements that would affect Redwood's liabilities or IP.
- Evidence onboarding: we can provide a named evidence custodian and agree to SLA windows for log retrieval; need to confirm the scope (e.g., retention window, PII redaction, export format).

Kimberly, can you propose language that preserves customer control but protects Redwood's interests? Connor — can you confirm turnaround time on evidence pulls for a production tenant in us-west-2?

I'll get back to Alyssa with a draft proposal by EOD PST.

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 14:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed defense-control / evidence wording for Faber MSA

Team —

I reviewed the redlines. Below is a concise, negotiable position we can propose to Faber that balances their request for customer-led defense with Redwood's need to limit downstream risk. Please treat as internal draft.

Proposed compromise (high level):
- Customer has primary defense control for third-party IP claims that relate solely to Customer's use of the Service.
- Redwood may assume control of the defense if Redwood reasonably concludes Customer's chosen counsel would materially prejudice Redwood's defense or rights.
- Settlement: Redwood's prior written consent required if settlement imposes an obligation on Redwood other than payment of money agreed in settlement capped at the indemnity cap.
- Cooperation: Both parties will cooperate in good faith; Redwood will provide technical evidence on a defined SLA (see Evidence Attachment).
- Evidence custodian: Redwood will designate a technical liaison and commit to retrieval windows: initial triage packet within 48 hours, forensic package within 7 calendar days (subject to scope and legal process).
- Confidentiality & redaction: Redwood may redact customer PII that is not necessary for defense; Redwood will provide a summary of redactions and make unredacted materials available under protective order.

Open negotiation points we should be prepared to trade on: escrow/insurance language, cap on fees, and allocation of discovery costs.

If we give Faber this language, I recommend adding a short playbook clause that sets an evidence-handling workflow and names Redwood's evidence custodian (Connor) + phone and escalation path. Connor, confirm the retrieval windows above. Marissa — please flag any procurement concessions we have recently accepted for references.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Evan Halley <ehalley@halleylaw.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@faberhealth.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA redlines - defense control and evidence onboarding

Ava / Alyssa —

FWIW from counsel's side: Faber needs customer control as a matter of procurement policy. They will accept a Redwood right to intervene, but the right to "assume control" is a non-starter without a narrow, objective trigger. Suggested language alternatives:

1) Redwood may assume control only if a court or arbitration panel requires it, or if Redwood can demonstrate a direct conflict with Redwood's existing IP rights (and provide immediate notice and an opportunity for Faber to cure).

2) If Redwood objects to counsel selection, escrow for defense costs or an independent mediator to resolve counsel disputes.

On evidence: Faber wants a 24-hour initial evidence window for high-priority logs. That is tight but possible for a triage summary. Forensics (full dumps) will need a signed DPA addendum and SLA of 5-10 business days depending on the data egress constraints.

Happy to take a short call Monday with Kimberly to resolve the trigger language.

Evan Halley
Partner, Halley & Co. LLP
Evan.Halley@halleylaw.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines - defense control and evidence onboarding

Alyssa / Evan / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the helpful alternatives, Evan. After internal alignment we propose the following compromise language for the MSA (to send to Faber as a redline):

- Customer-led defense: Faber will have primary control of the defense for third-party IP claims.
- Limited Redwood step-in: Redwood may assume control only if Redwood reasonably demonstrates that Customer counsel's strategy would materially and adversely prejudice Redwood's ownership of its pre-existing models or third-party obligations. The step-in trigger must be documented in writing with a short escalation window (48 hours) and subject to mediation if the parties cannot agree on counsel within 5 business days.
- Settlement: Any settlement that would (i) require Redwood to take or abstain from action that impacts Redwood's core model IP or (ii) impose an uncapped financial obligation on Redwood requires prior written consent.
- Evidence handling: Redwood will produce an initial triage summary within 24 hours for high-priority incidents and a scoped forensic package within 5 business days after execution of the DPA; Redwood's evidence custodian will redacted PII and provide an unredacted set under protective order.

If Faber accepts the above in principle, we can convert to redline and Emily from procurement can route the PO. If they push back on the step-in trigger being too broad, we can offer the court/arbitration-trigger alternative Evan suggested.

Proposed next step: 30-minute alignment call Tue 09:00 PT with Kimberly, Alyssa, and Evan to finalize redline language. Please confirm availability and I'll send a calendar invite + quick redline PDF.

Best,
